SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
MONDAY - APRIL 24, 2023 - 07:00 P.M.
SIERRA ROOM - CERRITOS CENTER FOR THE PERFORMING ARTS
18000 PARK PLAZA DRIVE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Public observation and participation in this meeting will be facilitated through the methods described below.
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in-person in the Sierra Room subject to posted COVID-19 protocols.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in-person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

minutes_text:
MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD MONDAY, APRIL
24, 2023, 7:00 P.M., IN THE SIERRA ROOM AT CERRITOS CENTER FOR THE PERFORMING
ARTS, 18000 PARK PLAZA DRIVE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor/Chair Barrows.

3.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Lynda P. Johnson
  Council/Agency Member Chuong Vo
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Naresh Solanki
  Mayor/Chair Bruce W. Barrows

4.  New Business

4A.  Review and consideration of Budget Study Session No. 1 – Updating the Cerritos City
  Council on the status of the City's 2023/2024 budget preparation process, and considering
  potential objectives for achieving the City Council's priority goals for the upcoming fiscal
  year and inclusion in the 2024 Cerritos Strategic Plan (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  City Attorney Bill Ihrke provided information related to potential conflicts of interest related
  to Councilmember Johnson’s participation in budget discussions concerning the City’s
  agreement for law enforcement services with Councilmember Johnson’s employer, the Los
  Angeles County Sheriff’s Department.

  A staff report was given by Peter Kemp, Budget Manager. A PowerPoint presentation was
  displayed.

  CONSENSUS (Barrows): Directed the City Manager to memorialize the titles of the City
  Council’s Fiscal Year 2023-24 Priority Goals, revised as follows: 1. Increase tree & street
  maintenance/repair, 2. Increase & augment sales tax revenue, 3. Enhance effectiveness
  and efficiencies of public safety programs, 4. Increase technology infrastructure/use, and 5.
  Increase fiscal transparency.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Sam Desai expressed support for various initiatives to balance the budget, expedite street
  maintenance projects, generate community input, and increase transit services.

  Jay Gray expressed support for broadcasting study sessions and increased notification for
  sewer projects which impact residents. He also commented on the upcoming sunset of the
  City’s current Eden system and the City Treasurer position.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the Mayor
  declared the public comments period closed.

4.  New Business (continued)

4A.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Johnson, to incorporate the consensus
  objectives and associated estimated costs of the Strategic Plan Goal Implementation Objectives,
  as presented in the associated agenda report, into the Fiscal Year 2023-24 preliminary budget
  document for review and consideration by the City Council during the upcoming budget study
  session process (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

5.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned at 8:07 p.m.
